15: Sympathetic vasoconstrictor fibers release norepinephrine, acting predominantly at vascular α receptors. The new scan restores the previously cropped option C.
20: Hypoxia increases renal EPO expression; EPO stimulates marrow erythropoiesis. The clearer copy restores the opposite RBC-production endings of C and D.
28: Androgens promote erythropoiesis and help explain higher average RBC counts in men. The restored options distinguish androgen effects from muscle mass.
34: Inhibiting repolarizing potassium channels prolongs the action potential and effective refractory period, the classic class III antiarrhythmic mechanism.
The restored stem asks for an increase. Sustained enhancement of L-type current can also prolong an action potential in some circumstances; A is the conventional best pharmacological mechanism.
51: The recovered stem explicitly decreases afterload at fixed preload and inotropy. Lower load permits faster fiber shortening; it does not increase the unloaded maximum velocity Vmax.
70: The pulmonary trunk (with the ascending aorta) forms the anterior relation of the transverse pericardial sinus. The SVC is posterior to the sinus.

The source's 'anteriorly adjacent' is interpreted as asking what lies anterior to the sinus. If read as asking what the sinus lies anterior to, SVC would instead fit; retain this wording qualification.
75: The clearer stem specifies the oblique pericardial sinus, whose anterior wall is the posterior surface of the left atrium.
76: The recovered posture is supine: Gray's Anatomy describes the cardiac base opposite T5–T8 when supine, descending approximately to T6–T9 when erect.
77: The recovered stem says EXCEPT. The inferior thoracic aperture is bounded posteriorly by T12, not T11; ribs 11–12 and the costal margin contribute.
93: The clearer stem specifies pulmonary artery and aorta. The truncus arteriosus gives rise to the proximal ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk after outflow septation.
95: Septum primum persists as the flap valve of the foramen ovale. The source's option B says septum secundum, whereas the ostium secundum develops by resorption in septum primum.
